title: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops regular values that appear after an Overwrite
observed_behavior: In one super-step, a reducer channel (Annotated[int, operator.add]) receives three writes in order: 5, Overwrite(10), 3. The update ends at 10; the '3' written after the Overwrite is silently discarded with no error or warning.
structure_focus: Overwrite mixed with regular writes to the same reducer channel in a single super-step
notes: Open, labels bug/external. The issue's own repro is channel-level (calls BinaryOperatorAggregate.update directly), not a graph; the fixture reconstructs the implied topology of three parallel START branches writing 5 / Overwrite(10) / 3 to one reducer key. A maintainer comment says this is expected behavior that is just not well documented, which is why this is classified as usage + a semantics/documentation gap rather than a framework defect; later comments propose a docs-only fix. The parallel write order is not guaranteed by the runtime, so the fixture shows the structure rather than deterministic ordering.
